backup_odb_subnet.rationale: Choosing the wrong backup subnet could route sensitive backup traffic through insecure or shared networks. Policies should enforce use of private, approved subnets to maintain isolation.

backup_subnet_cidr.description: CIDR range of the backup subnet.
backup_subnet_cidr.rationale: The CIDR range defines where backup traffic flows. If set to public ranges, backups could be exposed externally. Restricting to private CIDRs prevents leakage of sensitive data.

cidr.description: Network settings. CIDR to use for cluster IP allocation.
cidr.rationale: This controls IP allocation for the cluster. Using 0.0.0.0/0 or other public ranges exposes database nodes to the internet. Policies should enforce private ranges only.

cloud_vm_cluster_id.description:
The ID of the VM Cluster to create. This value is restricted
to (^[a-z]([a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$) and must be a maximum of 63
characters in length. The value must start with a letter and end with
a letter or a number.
cloud_vm_cluster_id.rationale: This is simply the cluster’s identifier. It doesn’t affect how the system behaves or how secure it is, it’s just a naming requirement enforced by Google Cloud.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Without a deletion policy, Terraform could accidentally destroy critical clusters. Enforcing “PREVENT” or “ABANDON” avoids accidental removal of production resources.

deletion_protection.description: Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the cluster. Deleting this cluster via terraform destroy or terraform apply will only succeed if this field is false in the Terraform state.
deletion_protection.rationale: Prevents accidental or malicious deletion of the cluster. Essential for production workloads to avoid catastrophic data loss.

display_name.description: User friendly name for this resource.
display_name.rationale: This is only a user‑friendly label. It doesn’t influence access control, networking, encryption, or any security‑related configuration.

exadata_infrastructure.rationale: This field points to an existing Exadata infrastructure resource. It doesn’t modify any security settings; it only links the VM cluster to its underlying hardware environment.

labels.description:
Labels or tags associated with the VM Cluster. 

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Labels are metadata used for organising and filtering resources. They don’t control permissions, network exposure, or data protection, so they have no direct security impact.

location.description: Resource ID segment making up resource 'name'. See documentation for resource type 'oracledatabase.googleapis.com/DbNode'.
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the cluster is deployed. Wrong regions may violate compliance or data residency requirements. Policies should enforce an approved region whitelist.

network.description:
The name of the VPC network.
Format: projects/{project}/global/networks/{network}
network.rationale: The VPC network defines isolation boundaries. Deploying into the wrong network could expose the cluster to untrusted traffic. Policies should enforce private, approved VPCs.

odb_network.description:
The name of the OdbNetwork associated with the VM Cluster.
Format:
projects/{project}/locations/{location}/odbNetworks/{odb_network}
It is optional but if specified, this should match the parent ODBNetwork of
the odb_subnet and backup_odb_subnet.
odb_network.rationale: ODB network selection affects routing of database traffic. Using an insecure or misconfigured network could expose sensitive data. Policies should enforce correct parent ODB networks.

odb_subnet.rationale: Subnet choice determines IP allocation. If misconfigured, nodes could be placed in public or shared subnets. Policies should enforce private subnets only.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: This specifies which GCP project the resource belongs to. While projects have their own IAM and boundaries, this field alone doesn’t change any security behaviour of the VM cluster.

properties.description: Various properties and settings associated with Exadata VM cluster.

properties.cluster_name.rationale: This is an internal cluster name used by Oracle systems. It doesn’t affect authentication, networking, or data protection, it’s purely informational.

properties.cpu_core_count.rationale: This controls how many CPU cores are allocated. It affects performance and capacity, not security controls or exposure.

properties.data_storage_size_tb.description: The data disk group size to be allocated in TBs.
properties.data_storage_size_tb.rationale: This sets the size of the storage pool. It doesn’t influence encryption, access, or network exposure.

properties.db_node_storage_size_gb.rationale: This adjusts local VM storage size. It doesn’t change any security posture; it’s a resource sizing parameter.

properties.db_server_ocids.rationale: These are identifiers for database servers. They don’t modify access, encryption, or network rules, they’re just references.

properties.disk_redundancy.description:
The type of redundancy. 
 Possible values:
 DISK_REDUNDANCY_UNSPECIFIED
HIGH
NORMAL
properties.disk_redundancy.rationale: Disk redundancy directly impacts resilience. Low redundancy increases risk of data loss if disks fail. Policies should enforce HIGH or NORMAL redundancy.

properties.gi_version.rationale: This specifies the Grid Infrastructure version. While versioning can matter for patching, this field itself doesn’t enforce or weaken security settings.

properties.hostname_prefix.description: Prefix for VM cluster host names.
properties.hostname_prefix.rationale: This sets a naming pattern for VM hostnames. It doesn’t affect authentication, networking, or data protection.

properties.license_type.description:
License type of VM Cluster. 
 Possible values:
 LICENSE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED
LICENSE_INCLUDED
BRING_YOUR_OWN_LICENSE
properties.license_type.rationale: This determines the licensing model (included vs BYOL). Licensing has no direct impact on security configuration or behaviour.

properties.local_backup_enabled.rationale: Local backups protect against accidental deletion or corruption. If disabled, recovery options are limited. Policies should enforce backups in secure storage locations.

properties.memory_size_gb.rationale: This sets the memory allocation for the cluster. It affects performance, not security.

properties.node_count.rationale: This defines how many database nodes exist. It doesn’t change access control, encryption, or network exposure, only cluster size.

properties.ocpu_count.description: OCPU count per VM. Minimum is 0.1.
properties.ocpu_count.rationale: This adjusts the number of Oracle CPUs. It’s a performance parameter and doesn’t influence security.

properties.sparse_diskgroup_enabled.rationale: Sparse disk groups are a storage optimisation feature. They don’t weaken or strengthen security.

properties.ssh_public_keys.description: SSH public keys to be stored with cluster.
properties.ssh_public_keys.rationale: SSH keys control administrator access. Weak or unauthorised keys can lead to compromise. Policies should enforce valid, unique keys and disallow insecure values.

properties.diagnostics_data_collection_o.description: Indicates whether diagnostic collection is enabled for the VM cluster
properties.diagnostics_data_collection_o.rationale: Diagnostic events may capture sensitive metadata. If exposed, attackers could gain insights into system behaviour. Policies should restrict unnecessary collection or enforce secure handling.

properties.diagnostics_data_collection_o.description: Indicates whether health monitoring is enabled for the VM cluster
properties.diagnostics_data_collection_o.rationale: Health monitoring exposes system metrics. While useful, it can reveal sensitive performance data. Policies should ensure monitoring is enabled only in approved environments.

properties.diagnostics_data_collection_o.description:
Indicates whether incident logs and trace collection are enabled for the VM
cluster
properties.diagnostics_data_collection_o.rationale: Incident logs may contain sensitive traces and error details. If exposed, attackers could gain insights into vulnerabilities. Policies should enforce secure storage and limit exposure.

properties.time_zone.description:
Represents a time zone from the
[IANA Time Zone Database](https://www.iana.org/time-zones).

properties.time_zone.id.description: IANA Time Zone Database time zone, e.g. "America/New_York".
properties.time_zone.id.rationale: This sets the time zone for the system. Time zone configuration doesn’t affect access, encryption, or network security.

properties.time_zone.version.description: IANA Time Zone Database version number, e.g. "2019a".
properties.time_zone.version.rationale: This specifies the version of the time zone database. It has no impact on security controls or behaviour.
